info.title: Application data is backup-enabled
info.description: android:allowBackup is absent, which defaults to true, so the app's data goes into cloud backups and device-to-device transfers. With targetSdkVersion 36, Android 12 and later leave it out of `adb backup`, so USB extraction needs a device older than Android 12.
info.impact: Locally stored credentials or PII travel with the user's cloud backup and to a new device, and are extractable over USB on devices older than Android 12.
info.recommendation: Set android:allowBackup="false", or exclude sensitive files with android:dataExtractionRules (android:fullBackupContent below Android 12).

reasons: Backup-extractable app data. Backup is a documented platform feature and on by default. What matters is what would be in the backup: name a credential in app storage and this becomes a real extraction path.

info.title: No network security config declared
info.description: The app declares neither android:networkSecurityConfig nor usesCleartextTraffic, so it relies on platform defaults and pins no domain. With targetSdkVersion 36 those defaults block cleartext HTTP and trust only system CAs.
info.impact: Without pinning, anyone who gets a CA trusted on the device can read and alter the app's TLS traffic.
info.recommendation: Declare a network security config that disables cleartext and pins the domains that carry sensitive traffic.

reasons: No certificate pinning. Pinning defends against an attacker who already controls a trusted CA or the device's trust store. Without one of those, TLS is still doing its job. It becomes a finding when paired with what the unpinned channel actually carries.

info.title: No screenshot protection: FLAG_SECURE is never set
info.description: Nothing in the app sets WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE, so every screen can be screenshotted or recorded and appears in the recent-apps snapshot.
info.impact: Credentials, balances or personal data on screen end up in screenshots, screen recordings and the task-switcher preview.
info.recommendation: Set FLAG_SECURE on the windows of screens that show credentials or account data.

reasons: Screen contents not protected from capture. Without FLAG_SECURE, what a screen shows can end up in screenshots, screen recordings and the task-switcher preview. That matters on screens showing credentials, card numbers or balances; on its own it is a hardening note.

info.title: SSL pinning bypass in asm/all/chall8.dart
info.description: The app implements SSL pinning using the 'http_certificate_pinning' package. A hook on 'HttpCertificatePinning.check' returning 'CONNECTION_SECURE' would bypass the pinning.
info.impact: Context for the network findings: interception for testing needs this check bypassed first.
info.recommendation: Keep pinning, and make sure every client that carries credentials goes through it.

info.title: Task hijacking (StrandHogg) possible on Android 10 and lower
info.description: minSdkVersion 24 lets the app run on Android versions before 11, and its task affinity is its package name "com.flutter_labs.all". There, another app can declare the same affinity, with allowTaskReparenting, and have its own activity shown in this app's task.
info.impact: On a device running Android 10 or lower, a malicious app can put a look-alike screen on top of this app's task, phishing credentials or keeping the real app from being shown.
info.recommendation: Raise minSdkVersion to 30, where Android fixed this. Until then, android:taskAffinity="" on the <application> mitigates the original attack, though not its runtime variant on unpatched Android 9 and lower.
